Mechanism cheatsheet

Applies to: SINGLE-VARIABLE SENSITIVITY of tbm_meta_us10_baseline_1m: vertical barrier T_max = 40 business days (vs 120). ALL other parameters identical. This is a DIAGNOSTIC, not an optimisation — headline output is g_max_observed and avg_uniqueness, NOT gate pass/fail.

1. Core formula tested

Same TBM meta-sizer; vertical barrier shortened 120 bd -> 40 bd

\[\mathrm{PT}=8\hat{\sigma},\quad \mathrm{SL}=4\hat{\sigma},\quad T_{\max}=40\,\text{bd} \;\;(\text{was }120) \]

Identical Martin §2.5 σ̂ (20d EMA-of-squared-absolute-change, γ=0.95), PT=8σ / SL=4σ (σ-multipliers auto-track, NOT re-calibrated absolutes), single τ=0.50, single feature-subset = ER+rest, κ=1.0σ, g_min=0.30.

Shorter label window ⇒ less overlap ⇒ higher average uniqueness. Algebraic prediction: avg_uniqueness ~0.07 → ~0.21; effective sample ~290 → ~870 distinct training units.

2. Triggering condition

Diagnostic tree on g_max_observed: >0.75 = effective-sample collapse was the cause (Stage-1 HAS value, re-tune T_max); <0.60 = no learnable conditional edge on ZN-post-2003 (Stage-1 at ceiling, pursue Stage-2 / multi-instrument); 0.60-0.75 = partial, schedule T_max ∈ {60, 80}.

\[g(m_t) \in [0.30,\,1.0] \quad\text{(same scaler; discriminates collapse vs no-signal)} \]

Cells in sweep: Single config internally (feat=ER_plus_rest, τ=0.50, T_max=40). Family accounting charges +8 to n_configs_searched (50 → 58) for the T_max axis as one further honest selection dimension.
